newsitem.title: SPAIN: Bank of Spain cuts key rate to 6.75 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Spain cuts key rate to 6.75 percent.

text.p: The Bank of Spain on Thursday announced the sixth reduction in its key money market interest rate this year, bringing it down to 6.75 percent from 7.25 percent.
Economists surveyed by Reuters on Wednesday had predicted that a strict 1997 budget presented by the government last week would persuade the central bank to cut rates.
Analysts had, however, been divided on whether the Bank of Spain would reduce rates by half a percentage point or a quarter percentage point.
The government presented strict 1997 accounts to parliament on Monday.

The budget is designed to cut the deficit to three percent of gross domestic product from a projected 4.4 percent this year and ensure Spain's place among the first wave of countries in the launch of a single European currency.
